Ten minutes with an AI helper can make you give up sooner.
Researchers gave people fraction problems. Some had ChatGPT open beside them.
The helped group scored higher at first.
Then, after problem twelve, the chatbot vanished.
Their accuracy dropped, and they skipped far more questions. The group without help kept going.
It repeated with reading questions, across more than twelve hundred people.
The team's explanation: instant answers teach us to expect instant answers.
Co-author Brian Christian still writes in a paper notebook every day.
Their fix isn't less AI. It's AI that teaches like a tutor.
